MUQATIL:63:9-11/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r4.claim: God does not delay a soul once its appointed time arrives and knows the hypocrites' good and bad deeds.

TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk describes a believer dying with wealth but unpaid zakat, unperformed Hajj, and unpaid dues to God; he asks to return, but death is not delayed.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r13.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r13.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p635/r13.claim: Abū Bakr transmits بما يعملون with yāʾ from ʿĀṣim; Ḥafṣ and the other readers use tāʾ.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r1.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p439/r1.claim: Sibawayh says lan governs the subjunctive; al-Khalīl derives it from lā plus an and says verbs require an explicit or implicit an to be subjunctive.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p439/r10.claim: If mā is relative, a pronoun is deleted; if it is a verbal noun, nothing is omitted.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r2.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p439/r2.claim: Sibawayh objects that an object can be fronted with lan but not with an embedded in a relative clause.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r3.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v4p439/r3.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān says an item tied to the object of invariant lan cannot be fronted; Abū Isḥāq rejects this as unprecedented.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v4p439/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says some Arabs use a jussive after lan, but Abu Jaʿfar says this is unknown.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p439/r5.claim: The hamza in yuʾakhkhir is written wāw because it follows ḍamma; it cannot be alif after anything but fatḥa, and lightening it yields wāw.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p439/r6.claim: The hamza cannot be made intermediate because it would tend toward alif, which requires a preceding fatḥa.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v4p439/r7.claim: When consecutive hamzas have the same vowel, Abu ʿAmr lightens by deleting one, with the remaining hamza signaling it.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p439/r8.claim: God knows and records people's deeds in order to repay them.

NAHHAS:v4p439/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p439/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p439/r9.claim: A preposition and its governed noun normally form a unit at the end; apparent fronting is construed as delayed.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p294/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p294/r1.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p294/r1.claim: Abū Bakr's transmission from ʿĀṣim reads يعملون in the third person; the prior singular النفس can represent many people, licensing agreement by meaning.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p294/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p294/r2.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p294/r2.claim: The other readers, including Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, address the audience directly with تعملون.

THALABI:v9p324/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p324/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p324/r2.claim: The final verb in 'God will not delay a soul' has a reported variation between ya and ta readings.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r7.claim: The clearest meaning is that God does not postpone death beyond its appointed term.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r8.claim: Alternatively, He does not delay punishment after death but hastens it in the grave.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r1.claim: God will not defer anyone whose appointed term arrives, meaning at death.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r2.claim: Ata says that if the dying person were returned, he would not pay alms or make pilgrimage, as in 6:28.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r3.claim: The exegetes take this as a general address to everyone who has done good or evil.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r4.speaker: عاصم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p480/r4.claim: Asim reads يعملون in the third person, because نفس is singular in form but refers to many people in meaning.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r3.claim: God will not delay a soul once its appointed time comes.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r1.claim: Lifespans are recorded and neither advance nor recede; people should not rely on extra time after neglect, since they waste much time and then wish for a little more.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r2.claim: If the dead were returned while compelled to know the truth, they could not be returned because they would be coerced; without compulsion, they would be like someone waking and resume their former ways, as 6:28 says.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r3.claim: God knows their deeds and will recompense them for them.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r8.claim: The statement that God will not delay anyone's term indicates that each person has one appointed lifespan, whether death occurs naturally or by killing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p135/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p135/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p135/r1.claim: Abū Bakr reads يعملون in third person; the others read تعملون in second person.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546#2/r1.claim: A report promises freedom from hypocrisy for whoever recites Surat al-Munafiqun.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r12.claim: The emphatic denial that God delays a soul means such delay would conflict with wisdom; knowing death is unavoidable and deeds judged requires prompt fulfillment of duties and readiness to meet God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p546/r13.claim: The closing verb is also read with either second-person plural or third-person plural inflection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#3/r5.claim: The warning urges people to act before their appointed time; most read taʿmalūn addressing everyone, while ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr reads yaʿmalūn to single out the disbelievers.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r12.claim: The fixed term is the absolute time God decrees for a living person to die; a conditional term may be extended, shortened, or interrupted according to the benefit God knows.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r13.claim: The verse connects to what precedes it: God would extend people's term if He knew they would repent, but He knows they will not.

TABRISI:63:11/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11/r6.claim: The third-person reading treats ‘a soul’ as plural in meaning despite its singular form; the second-person reading is a general address.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p278/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p278/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p278/r1.claim: God knows what people do, including hypocrites' denial of charity.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf says that God will not delay a soul is an emphatic negation whose force excludes any postponement.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r5.claim: If the dead were returned to worldly life, they would return to their former forbidden behavior, as 6:28 says.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r6.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r6.claim: Commentators understand God's knowledge of what people do to encompass every good and bad deed.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r7.speaker: عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim reads yaʿmalūn with yāʾ, carrying the grammatical singular 'soul' according to its collective meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r2.claim: God knows the good and evil people do.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r3.speaker: قراءة العامة
QURTUBI-FULL:63:10-11#2/r3.claim: The common reading uses tāʾ as direct address; Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim and al-Sulamī read yāʾ as reporting what the dead person said.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r1.claim: God gives no soul a reprieve once its lifespan ends; He knows deeds and recompenses them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r2.claim: Abū Bakr reads the verb with ياء, matching the preceding third-person phrasing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:11/r3.claim: A report says that whoever recites Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn is freed from hypocrisy; no grading is stated.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.claim: No soul's appointed death, written in the Preserved Tablet, will be postponed.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.claim: A variant reads “they do” instead of “you do”; knowing that death cannot be delayed and deeds will be requited should prompt people to fulfill obligations and prepare to meet God.

QASHANI:63:9-11/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:63:9-11/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:63:9-11/r3.claim: At death, wealth belongs to heirs, so last-minute giving yields only regret; sincere belief recognizes death as necessary at its appointed time and cannot expect delay.

QASHANI:63:9-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:63:9-11/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:63:9-11/r4.claim: God knows intentions, so a dying person’s promised charity is futile when it comes from miserliness and love of money rather than generosity; such wishes are lies, as another verse says.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r10.claim: The statement that God will not delay a soul when its term arrives urges haste in obedience before death comes without preparation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r11.claim: Most read تعملون addressing everyone; Abū Bakr reads third person as a threat to unbelievers, perhaps still general.

SAMIN-DURR:63:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:11/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
SAMIN-DURR:63:11/r1.claim: Abu Bakr reads بما يعملون in third person; the other readers address the audience directly.

SAMIN-DURR:63:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:63:11/r2.speaker: أبي وعبد الله وابن جبير
SAMIN-DURR:63:11/r2.claim: They read فأتصدق, the unassimilated source form of the common reading, whose tāʾ merges into ṣād.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says Sufyan ibn Uyayna and others transmit Ibn Abbas’s statement in stopped form, which is sounder, and he weakens Abu Janab; al-Dahhak’s report from Ibn Abbas is disconnected.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133#2/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133#2/r2.claim: The Prophet said God does not delay a soul after its term; an apparent increase in lifespan comes when God grants a person righteous children whose prayers reach him in the grave.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r3.claim: Once a person’s appointed term arrives, God gives no extension; He knows who would sincerely reform and who would return to worse conduct if sent back.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p615#2/r8.claim: God will not postpone any soul once its appointed time arrives; the verse’s final warning includes the speaker and all other people.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p617/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p617/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p617/r1.claim: The closing claim that God knows human conduct is linked to 67:14, which asks whether the Creator would not know what He created.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.claim: The Prophet says a person able to perform pilgrimage or owing zakat who neglects it will ask to return at death; Ibn Abbas supports the warning by reciting the whole surah.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a dying believer who withheld zakat, pilgrimage dues, or another due to God will ask to return and give charity and zakat; God will not delay the appointed term.

BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437#2/r8.claim: God does not defer anyone, obedient or sinful, young or old, once the appointed term comes; ‘term’ can mean the life span or its final moment.

BURSEVI:v9p438/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p438/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p438/r1.claim: Some infer the Prophet’s lifespan from this being the sixty-third sūrah, followed by al-Taghābun, displaying the loss caused by his departure.

BURSEVI:v9p438/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p438/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p438/r2.claim: Some distinguish ordinary unavoidable death at the fixed term from chosen spiritual death during worldly life, associated with unifying knowledge that lifts veils; direct vision brings felicity to ordinary believers.

BURSEVI:v9p438/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p438/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p438/r3.claim: The spiritually dead are ‘dead but not dead,’ like martyrs who are killed rather than dead; one who kills the ego in the greater struggle receives martyrdom’s spiritual rank while alive.

BURSEVI:v9p438/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p438/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p438/r4.claim: God knows and repays deeds, good for good and evil for evil, so believers should hasten to good and prepare for what is coming.

BURSEVI:v9p438/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p438/r5.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v9p438/r5.claim: Faith requires God’s love to outweigh all else; attachment to people and wealth can veil believers and squander innate capacity on what quickly perishes.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r1.claim: God will not give a soul respite once its appointed term arrives; ajal may mean the final lifespan or the span allotted from beginning to end.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r2.claim: Abū Bakr reads the verb with yāʾ, in third person, matching the preceding verse's third-person style.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r3.claim: Because nafsan is indefinite in a negative context, it has universal force, meaning no person is excepted.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that the commands to spend, the wish for a reprieve, and God's refusal to delay refute determinism; al-Ālūsī answers that the commands do not prove freedom, the wish is no evidence, and the reply merely frustrates the wish.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p118#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the determinist debate is irrelevant to the orthodox, and none of the cited statements proves the point claimed.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r12.claim: God knows every deed, rewarding those who remember and spend for Him and punishing those who forget Him and plunge into worldly life.

ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11#2/r13.claim: This profit and loss becomes clear on the Day of Account and Mutual Loss, and the chapter is followed by Sūrat al-Taghābun.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r1.claim: خبير is preferred to عليم because it conveys knowledge of hidden matters, including inward resolve and intention as well as outward deeds.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r2.claim: Death interrupting a good deed whose legally appointed time remains open does not deprive a believer of its reward, including a regular devotional practice or intended Hajj.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r3.claim: A believer who regularly performs a devotional portion or resolves to do good but is prevented receives its reward.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r4.claim: He cites an authentic hadith that a good deed intended but left undone is recorded as one complete good deed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r5.claim: The majority read تعملون with second-person ت, addressing the listeners.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r6.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p256/r6.claim: This reader uses third-person ي; its pronoun refers to the generic singular نفسا, which has plural sense in the negation.

TABATABAI:63:11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:11/r1.claim: The phrase that God knows what people do is either a circumstantial clause or a renewed sentence serving as a reason: do not be distracted, and spend, since God knows and recompenses deeds.

TABATABAI:63:11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:11/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:63:11/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says God has deferred records from which He advances or delays what He wills; on the Night of Decree He sends what will occur through the next year, and what is written in the heavenly book is not delayed.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r11.claim: Once a person's appointed term arrives, God will not delay it; this ends hope for postponement after death has come and the signs of the next life appear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.claim: The closing three verses warn Muslims not to let wealth and children distract from remembering God; those who fail to spend for God's cause will regret it after death, when regret is useless.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.claim: The first section identifies worldly love as the root of hypocrisy; the second urges Muslims to guard against that same cause.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p338/r6.claim: The deathbed wish for time remains futile: God does not extend a soul’s term, and He knows that the promise of future charity is baseless.

QIRAAT-ER:63:11:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:63:11:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:63:11:14#1/r1.claim: The third-person plural shifts from direct audience address to reference about a group.

STUDYQURAN:63:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r1.claim: These verses indicate that zakāh should be paid promptly and obligatory religious duties should not be delayed.

STUDYQURAN:63:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r3.claim: When a person’s appointed term comes, death arrives and the door of repentance closes.

STUDYQURAN:63:10/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r4.claim: The warning follows the sūrah’s theme of hypocrisy: although sincere repentance is possible before death, one should not deliberately wait until death to repent.

STUDYQURAN:63:10/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r5.claim: God grants every soul time to repent out of mercy and forgiveness; otherwise, human beings would be wiped from the earth for their deeds.

STUDYQURAN:63:10/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:10/r6.claim: Those who deliberately postpone repentance and good deeds until death receive no reprieve once their term arrives.
